description: Figure 8 displays three pie charts illustrating the distribution of problem difficulty—labeled as easy, medium, and hard—based on the correctness of model responses under two different settings: with knowledge (w/ knowledge) and without knowledge (w/o knowledge), both using a zero-shot approach. The chart on the left, labeled "easy," shows the distribution for easy problems, with a large teal segment representing 55.4% (N+K+) and a smaller orange segment representing 4.6% (N-K-). The middle chart, labeled "medium," shows the distribution for medium problems, with a large teal segment at 58.8% (N+K+) and a smaller orange segment at 4.8% (N-K-). The chart on the right, labeled "hard," shows the distribution for hard problems, with a large teal segment at 37.3% (N+K+), a medium-sized yellow segment at 37.9% (N-K+), a smaller orange segment at 18.1% (N-K-), and a small red segment at 6.7% (N+K-). A legend in the top right corner indicates that the teal color represents the N+K+ setting, yellow represents N-K+, orange represents N-K-, and red represents N+K-. The percentages are labeled within each slice of the pie charts.
